es.summary: La dopamina es un agente inotrópico y vasopresor usado en hipotensión grave y shock para mejorar gasto cardíaco y perfusión tisular.
key_points: Efectos dependen de la dosis: bajas dosis → dopaminérgicos renales, medias → β1, altas → α1.
Se administra por infusión intravenosa continua, titrando según presión arterial y gasto cardíaco.
Monitorear presión arterial media (PAM), ritmo cardíaco y diuresis cada 15‑30 min al iniciar.
Contraindicada en feocromocitoma y taquiarritmias no controladas.
Efectos adversos comunes: taquicardia, arritmias, vasoconstricción periférica que puede causar isquemia.

mechanism: Activa receptores dopaminérgicos (D1) en riñón → vasodilatación renal y aumento de flujo.
A dosis medias estimula β1 → aumenta frecuencia y contractilidad cardíaca.
A dosis altas estimula α1 → vasoconstricción sistémica, eleva presión arterial.
indications: Hipotensión severa o shock que no responde a fluidos.
Insuficiencia cardíaca con bajo gasto y necesidad de soporte inotrópico.
Situaciones perioperatorias con riesgo de bajo gasto cardíaco.
contraindications: Obstrucción mecánica de la vía aérea o shock séptico avanzado sin reposición volémica adecuada.
adverse_effects: Isquemia distal o necrosis del tejido (serio).
interactions: Inhibidores de MAO pueden potenciar efectos catecolaminérgicos.
Beta‑bloqueadores pueden atenuar la respuesta β1 de la dopamina.
Diuréticos pueden aumentar riesgo de hipotensión si la dosis es insuficiente.
nursing_care: Verificar orden, concentración y velocidad de infusión antes de iniciar.
Obtener línea IV de calibre adecuado (18‑20G) y conectar a bomba de infusión.
Monitorear PAM, frecuencia cardíaca y ritmo cada 5‑15 min al iniciar y después de ajustes.
Registrar diuresis; suspender si <0.5 mL/kg/h y notificar al médico.
Retener la infusión y notificar si PAM <65 mmHg, arritmia significativa o signos de isquemia.
patient_teaching: Explicar que la bomba de infusión es continua y no debe interrumpirse sin indicación.
Informar sobre posibles sensaciones de palpitaciones o temblores y reportarlas.
Enseñar la importancia de mantener la vía IV libre y sin obstrucciones.
Indicar que se controlarán signos vitales frecuentemente; colaborar permaneciendo en reposo.
antidote_overdose: No hay antídoto específico; manejo de sobredosis con soporte hemodinámico y reducción de la velocidad de infusión.
En caso de arritmia grave, considerar antiarrítmicos según protocolo y monitorización continua.

en.summary: Dopamine is an inotropic and vasopressor agent used in severe hypotension and shock to improve cardiac output and tissue perfusion.
key_points: Effects depend on dose: low doses → renal dopaminergic effects, moderate doses → β1, high doses → α1.
Administered by continuous intravenous infusion, titrated according to blood pressure and cardiac output.
Monitor mean arterial pressure (MAP), heart rate, and urine output every 15‑30 min at initiation.
Contraindicated in pheochromocytoma and uncontrolled tachyarrhythmias.
Common adverse effects: tachycardia, arrhythmias, peripheral vasoconstriction that may cause ischemia.

mechanism: Activates dopaminergic receptors (D1) in kidney → renal vasodilation and increased flow.
At moderate doses stimulates β1 → increases heart rate and contractility.
At high doses stimulates α1 → systemic vasoconstriction, raising blood pressure.
indications: Severe hypotension or shock unresponsive to fluids.
Heart failure with low output and need for inotropic support.
Perioperative situations with risk of low cardiac output.
contraindications: Mechanical airway obstruction or advanced septic shock without adequate volume resuscitation.
interactions: MAO inhibitors can potentiate catecholamine effects.
Beta‑blockers can blunt dopamine’s β1 response.
Diuretics may increase risk of hypotension if dose is insufficient.
nursing_care: Verify order, concentration, and infusion rate before starting.
Obtain an appropriately sized IV line (18‑20G) and connect to infusion pump.
Monitor MAP, heart rate, and rhythm every 5‑15 min at initiation and after adjustments.
Record urine output; discontinue if <0.5 mL/kg/h and notify the provider.
Hold the infusion and notify if MAP <65 mmHg, significant arrhythmia, or signs of ischemia.
patient_teaching: Explain that the infusion pump is continuous and should not be interrupted without indication.
Inform about possible sensations of palpitations or tremors and to report them.
Teach the importance of keeping the IV line clear and unobstructed.
Indicate that vital signs will be monitored frequently; encourage rest and cooperation.
antidote_overdose: No specific antidote; manage overdose with hemodynamic support and reduction of infusion rate.
In case of severe arrhythmia, consider antiarrhythmics per protocol and continuous monitoring.

sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Cardiac Emergency Drugs

summary.0.quote: Dopamine is used in profound hypotension and shock to increase cardiac output by increasing the rate and force of contraction and blood pressure by vasoconstriction.

key_points.1.quote: Titration parameters include blood pressure and signs of tissue perfusion (adequate urine output).

key_points.3.quote: Contraindications to the use of dopamine include pheochromocytoma, uncorrected tachyarrhythmias or ventricular fibrillation, and allergy to metabisulfite.

key_points.4.quote: Dopamine can cause ventricular arrhythmia, atrial fibrillation, ectopic beats, tachycardia, anginal pain, palpitations, cardiac conduction abnormalities, widened QRS complex, bradycardia, hypotension, hypertension, vasoconstriction, dyspnea, azotemia, headache, and anxiety.

sections.mechanism.1.quote: Directly stimulates beta-1 receptors in the heart, which increases contractility and heart rate

sections.indications.1.quote: Indications Short-term inotropic support for cardiac decompensation

sections.contraindications.0.quote: Contraindications to the use of dopamine include pheochromocytoma, uncorrected tachyarrhythmias or ventricular fibrillation, and allergy to metabisulfite.

sections.contraindications.1.quote: Contraindications to the use of dopamine include pheochromocytoma, uncorrected tachyarrhythmias or ventricular fibrillation, and allergy to metabisulfite.

sections.adverse_effects.1.quote: Epinephrine can cause anxiety and excitability, headache, fear, heart palpitations, tachycardia, supraventricular tachycardia, ventricular arrhythmias, hypertension, cerebral hemorrhage, hemiplegia, subarachnoid hemorrhage, anginal pain in clients with angina, pulmonary edema, hypoglycemia, hypokalemia, and lactic acidosis.

sections.adverse_effects.2.quote: At high doses, dopamine causes vasoconstriction, which increases blood pressure.

sections.adverse_effects.4.quote: Extravasation of dopamine into the tissue around an IV site may cause necrosis, sloughing, and potentially gangrene.
